steps.message:
# Reconcile the reservations of kit orders

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server. Free stock is in the warehouse `main`, and units held for open sales orders are in the warehouse `reserved`.

The component reservations of several kit and bundle orders no longer match the orders. Reconcile them. Everything you need is in `/app/kits/`:

- `policy.md`: how reservations, releases and picks are posted, how kits explode into components, which revision of a kit applies, how order lines are amended, and which substitutions are allowed. Follow it.
- `open-orders.csv`: the orders to reconcile, one row per amendment of an order line: order id, line, amendment number, the date the order was created, the sku ordered (a kit or a stocked sku), the quantity and the status.
- `kit-bom.csv`: the components of each kit by revision, with the date each revision took effect.

What to do:

1. For every order in `open-orders.csv`, make the reservation the order holds for each sku equal to what the policy says it should hold. Use `adjust_stock` with the order id as reference, as the policy describes. Some reservations are right, and some are not.
2. Write `/app/kit-reservations.csv`, a CSV file with the header `order,sku,required,picked,reserved` and one row for each order in `open-orders.csv` and each sku that the order requires or that has a posting in `reserved` under the order, including rows that need no change. All three quantities are in each: `required` is the units of the sku the order requires, `picked` the units picked under the order that count toward the sku, and `reserved` the reservation the order holds for the sku when you are done.

Do not change anything for orders that are not in `open-orders.csv`, and do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

arguments.command: cd /app/kits; cat policy.md; cat open-orders.csv; cat kit-bom.csv

results.content:
# Kit orders: reservations, picks and reconciliation

## Warehouses and postings

Free stock is kept in the warehouse `main`. Units held for an open sales order are kept in the
warehouse `reserved`. Every posting below is an `adjust_stock` call with the order id (`SO-...`) as
reference. All quantities are in each, the stock unit of every component.

- Reservation: the quantity out of `main` and the same quantity into `reserved`, both with reason
  `transfer`.
- Release: the quantity out of `reserved` and the same quantity into `main`, both with reason
  `transfer`.
- Pick: one adjustment with reason `shipment` and a negative delta. Pickers take reserved units out
  of `reserved`. A unit taken from the shelf instead, and every substitute, is posted out of `main`.
  Both count as picked for the order.

The reservation an order holds for a sku is the net of all postings in `reserved` with that sku and
the order's reference: reservations, minus releases, minus picks out of `reserved`.

## Kits

Kits and bundles are not stocked. `kit-bom.csv` lists the components of each kit by revision. A
component of a kit can itself be a kit: explode it as well, multiplying the quantities down the
tree, until only stocked skus remain. A sku that is not a kit in `kit-bom.csv` is stocked, and an
order line for it reserves the sku itself.

A revision applies from its `effective_from` date, that day included, until the next revision of
the same kit takes effect. Every kit in an order's tree, nested kits included, uses the revision in
effect on the date the order was created, whatever revision is in effect today.

## Order lines

`open-orders.csv` has one row per amendment of an order line. Amendment 0 is the line as it was
entered. The row with the highest amendment number of a line is in effect and replaces the earlier
rows of that line. A line whose row in effect has status `cancelled` requires nothing.

## Substitutions

A picker may ship a substitute in place of a component only where this table allows it, for the kit
whose bill of materials lists the component. `ratio` units of the substitute replace one unit of
the component.

| kit | component | substitute | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| KT-10 | CP-202 | CP-213 | 1 |
| KT-10 | CP-203 | CP-214 | 2 |
| KT-20 | CP-204 | CP-218 | 1 |

A substitute pick counts toward the component when the order's tree holds a kit that allows that
substitution. Otherwise it counts toward nothing, and the component it replaced is still required.
Substitutes are never reserved.

## Reconciliation

For each order and each sku:

1. Required: the units of the sku that the order's lines in effect require, after exploding kits.
2. Picked: the units of the sku picked under the order, plus the substitute picks that count toward
   it, divided by their ratio.
3. The order should hold the required units minus the picked units in `reserved`, and nothing when
   more was picked than is required. Reserve what is missing. Release the excess, including the
   whole reservation of a sku the order no longer requires.

steps.reasoning_content: I need every adjustment for each order reference, and there are 17 orders. Filtering by reference with 5 per page means several pages for each one, so I'll make the calls per order and run them in parallel.

The paging is getting heavy with 17 orders and many pages per order, so I'm checking whether there's a local database file I could read directly, though that's probably not available. I'm also considering filtering by warehouse and reference to cut down the volume, but I still need the main-warehouse picks, so I'll keep paging through the results.

Next I'm fetching page 1 for the unknown order totals in 5507-5512, and I'll keep going through the remaining pages for the known ones.

I'm fetching the remaining pages for the batch: 5504 pages 2 through 6, 5507 pages 2 through 4, page 2 of 5508, 5509 pages 2 through 5, 5510 pages 2 through 5, 5511 pages 2 through 3, and page 2 of 5512.

I'm going to compute this with a short script rather than by hand. Next I'm tallying the reserved nets and picks per order, starting with order 5501, which has reservations for six CP items, each at 3, and several pick reversals.

I'm checking the reserved quantities for order 5501 against the picks, and 202 comes up short, so it needs one unit released. I'm moving on to 5502, where the reservation rolls to the later revision and the held counts need adjusting for 206, 211 and 212. Then I'll look at 5503 and its component holds and the direct pick on CP-216.

I'm working through order 5504 now: it's a KT-40 on 08-28, built from a KT-30 and a KT-20 plus a direct line on 205. Counting down the components, KT-10 and KT-20 together push the requirement for 204 to 4, and I'm tallying the rest of the part quantities from there.

I'm checking the remaining targets for order 5504: the counts for 205, 211, 215 and 216 line up with the earlier requirements, and 201 and 215 are already picked from reserved stock. Working out the reserved net on 201 and 204 now, since the KT-20 substitution from CP-218 changes how much of 204 is still needed.

I'm checking the held and reserved quantities for orders 5505 and 5506 now, starting with the KT-20 amendment that drops the quantity to 2 and lines up CP-205 at 4. After that I'll write the rest of the data out so the script can run the full reconciliation.

I'm checking the order 5506 holds against the amended requirement, where only CP-207 stays at 2 and the other seven items get released. Then I'm turning to order 5507, a KT-10 on 08-30, where I'm sorting out the reserved picks and the net on CP-204 so I can see how much is still needed.

I'm settling the order 5507 reserve on CP-204 at one unit, and then I'm checking 5508, where the KT-20 amendment leaves 207 and 208 and 204 with held counts above what's required, so those get released. Next I'm moving on to 5509, a KT-10 for two units dated 09-09, which means the later revision applies, and I'm looking at the holds on 201 through 206 and 212.

I'm checking order 5510 next: it's a KT-30 for one unit on 09-11, so the later KT-10 revision applies. Its component holds look right against the requirements, with 201 through 206 and 212 at one each, and 215, 216, 217 and 209 covered too, so nothing needs adjusting there.

I'm checking the order 5511 reservations next: the 09-04 and 09-11 postings both add to 204, 207 and 208, and the picks bring the held counts down to match what's required. Then I'm moving on to order 5512, a KT-20 for one unit on 09-12, which falls under the later revision.

I'm wrapping up the reconciliation by listing the corrective actions for each order: releasing surplus holds, reserving the missing quantities, and checking the 5503 rows where 216 needs four against two picked.

I'm checking the 5503 rows once more, and the KT-10 line for sku 204 needs no substitution, so that one is settled. Next I'm confirming that main stock covers all the pending reserve and release moves, and I'll run those operations in parallel since the pairs don't depend on each other.
I'm now working through the reserves for SKU 5503, which takes two calls for each of its seven SKUs, and then moving on to 5505 through 5509 and 5512. It's a large batch.

Next I'm moving on to the CSV output, and I'll use Python to compute it from the data I've already derived. Each row will cover one order/SKU pair, showing the required quantity, the picked quantity, and the final reserved quantity taken from the required or reserved postings. I'll write the script for that now.

I'm checking the 5506 rows, since the SKUs with released postings (201-206, 212) are missing because my reserved dict only had 207. I'll add 5506 and then verify 5508, where the required and picked counts don't match.

Checking the SKU entries for the 5506 rows now.

steps.message:
I reconciled the reservations for all 17 orders in `open-orders.csv` and wrote `/app/kit-reservations.csv` and `/app/STATUS.json` (status `success`). I did not re-read the inventory after posting. The CSV is computed from the postings I read before I changed anything, plus the adjustments I made. Every `adjust_stock` call succeeded.

Each adjustment is a pair of `transfer` postings between `main` and `reserved`, with the order id as reference.

| Order | Change |
|---|---|
| SO-5501 | released 1 of CP-202 |
| SO-5502 | released 2 of CP-211; reserved 2 each of CP-206 and CP-212 |
| SO-5503 | released 2 of CP-216; reserved 2 each of CP-201 to CP-206 and CP-212 |
| SO-5504 | released 1 of CP-204; reserved 2 of CP-207 and 1 of CP-208 |
| SO-5505 | released 1 of CP-204, 2 of CP-207 and 1 of CP-208 |
| SO-5506 | released 2 each of CP-201 to CP-206 and CP-212 |
| SO-5507 | reserved 1 of CP-204 |
| SO-5508 | released 3 of CP-207, 2 of CP-208 and 2 of CP-204 |
| SO-5509 | released 1 of CP-203 |
| SO-5512 | reserved 1 of CP-210 |
| SO-5510, SO-5511 | already correct, no change |

Some of these follow from policy rules that are easy to miss:
- **SO-5502:** it was created on 2026-09-03, so KT-10 revision B applies, not revision A.
- **SO-5506:** line 1 was cancelled by its amendment, so only the CP-207 line remains.
- **SO-5507:** the CP-218 pick doesn't count toward anything, because KT-10 doesn't allow it as a substitute. That is why CP-204 still needs a reservation.
- **SO-5508:** it was created on 2026-09-08, before KT-20 revision B took effect, so revision A applies.

The CSV has 76 rows plus the header, including rows for SKUs that an order no longer requires and whose reservation is now zero.
